we are able to probe the ultrafast evolution of electric field pulses from high intensity laser matter interactions and we are able to differentiate the contribution by the forerunner and the radiated pulses.
we are able to measure the evolution of the electromagnetic field generated from laser-matter interactions in the time domain.

the evolution of the electric field and the electron bunches is strongly dependent on the target material.

the interaction of ultra-short high-intense laser pulses with solid targets is not a simple one-step process but a complicated multi-step one that involves the generation of a high-energy electron bunch that propagates through the target and the emission of an electromagnetic pulse by the remaining charges.
